content:
In early July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed, but the same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't significantly affected by this bug. So initially, I assumed this TestFlight update was a simple yet meaningful improvement.

Sometimes, a small change can have a major impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta apps, and the latest TestFlight update is a perfect example. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds a "search bar for users to quickly search for apps."

In retrospect, I did notice some strange phenomena, which I also mentioned at the bottom of the article (although my understanding at the time was completely the opposite):

I believe the reason I didn't realize this was a bug is that I kept all the TestFlight beta apps I've installed over the years, with the purpose of "merging" my previously separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It's not the most convenient approach, but for me, it was worth it.

In any case, this TestFlight bug did not escape the notice of John Vorhees from MacStories:

So you can imagine how excited I was when I saw Zac Hall writing an article on 9to5Mac about the new search bar added to TestFlight. I thought to myself at the time: "Finally!" I immediately put down what I was doing and went to update the app. [...] Unfortunately, there's a big "but" here. Previously, beta versions in TestFlight were sorted in reverse chronological order, which I personally really liked. [...] Now, expired beta versions and still-active TestFlight betas are mixed together in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a rough count, and for me, there are about 800 app entries. As you can imagine, only a very small fraction of these are actually active betas. The search function does help, but it is no longer possible to scroll through to find items.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote on Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and this bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and after it was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update does indeed fix the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix provided for users affected by this regression issue.
